clue.text: What percussionists do to get publicity

definitions.meaning: idiom for campaigning loudly to promote a cause or product

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the action of a drummer at work, and figuratively an idiom for noisily promoting something.

clue.text: The milk apiarists try to avoid

definitions.text: The milk apiarists try to avoid

parts.words: The milk apiarists try to avoid
parts.note: read as insect stings that beekeepers dodge, but the word also names the first milk a cow gives after calving

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the word as bee + stings, which beekeepers (apiarists) naturally avoid; really it is the rich first milk from a newly calved cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is a dairy word for colostrum, the first milk a cow produces after giving birth.

clue.text: Football team's armoury

explanation.walkthrough: ARSENAL is a Premier League football club from north London, named after the Royal Arsenal at Woolwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known North London football club, and also a store or collection of weapons.

clue.text: Actor has little right to upset old Scotsman

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting a piece turns it upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: RT is a short form of right
aged means old
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A performer with few rights is moved to upset an elderly man from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to upset' means turned upside down, so the short form of right is read from bottom to top; 'has' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is a stage performer who specialises in tragic roles.

clue.text: Those stockpiled weapons include a sword

indicators.note: the clue words are said to contain the answer, which runs across the boundary between Those and stockpiled

explanation.surface: A hoard of arms happens to contain one blade.
explanation.definitionFit: An estoc is a long thrusting sword of medieval Europe.

clue.text: Mature east German entered with rejoinder

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as if walking into it

parts.note: ripe means mature
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: An older East German came in carrying a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp reply, a synonym of a retort.

clue.text: Grain processed on a holiday island

parts.note: malt is grain, usually barley, that has been steeped and dried

explanation.surface: Cereal treated on a Mediterranean holiday destination.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean island nation that is a popular sunshine destination for tourists.

clue.text: Hopes to find articulate Indian worshippers

indicators.note: articulate means spoken clearly, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: Sikhs are followers of a religion founded in the Punjab, India

explanation.surface: Wishes to locate well-spoken religious believers from India.
explanation.definitionFit: To look for something in the hope of finding it; a synonym of searching.

clue.text: He may discard wood with hesitation

definitions.text: He may discard wood with hesitation

parts.note: to scrap something is to throw it away
deal is pine or fir timber
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A man who reluctantly throws timber away.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is a crossword favourite for softwood timber. The whole clue also describes the trader, who sells on what others throw out.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader in waste metal and discarded goods, who buys junk and sells it on.

clue.text: George, Paul, Otto and I are devastated

indicators.note: being devastated means wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Four men named George, Paul and Otto, plus the speaker, are all distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is British slang, originally from RAF pilots, for an aircraft's automatic pilot; it looks like a fourth person in the list. 'and' just joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British pilots' slang name for the automatic flight-control system.

clue.text: Go ahead and strip church roof

definitions.meaning: literally removing the metal sheeting from a church roof, a common theft

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for moving into first place, and literally stealing the metal covering from a church roof.

clue.text: Regret transporting English money by train

indicators.note: carrying something inside it, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: rue means regret
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A sorry passenger carries pounds on a railway journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A train in the sense of an entourage, the attendants following an important person.

clue.text: Old cavalryman made officers fire

parts.note: COs are commanding officers
to sack means to dismiss from a job

explanation.surface: A veteran horseman led his commanders into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Russian and Ukrainian horsemen famed as light cavalry under the tsars.

clue.text: Sheet of glass left on board

parts.note: a pane is one sheet of window glass

explanation.surface: A glazed sheet resting on a wooden plank.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a flat piece of wood or other material, a synonym for a board.

clue.text: The paints must be stirred once

indicators.note: stirring paint mixes it about, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Decorators are reminded to mix their tins before use.
explanation.definitionFit: Once in the sense of formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Appearing in a shorter skirt, maybe

definitions.meaning: folding up a hem shortens a skirt

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for arriving or showing up, and literally folding a hem higher to shorten clothing.

clue.text: Adjunct makes a parish priest finish on time

parts.note: end means finish
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An extra duty makes a local cleric wrap up punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something added on to a larger thing, a synonym for an attachment.

clue.text: Each contract gained by tougher new yorker, perhaps

parts.note: ea is the shortened, contracted form of each
sterner means tougher or harsher

explanation.surface: Every deal is won by a harder bargainer from New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gained by' just links the pieces. The definition's 'perhaps' shows a New Yorker is one example: someone from the eastern United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the eastern part of a country; someone from New York is an example in the United States.

clue.text: Speak sharply when presented with outdated demand

parts.note: ex means former, no longer current
a claim is a demand for something as one's right

explanation.surface: Shout out when faced with an old-fashioned request.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, a synonym of calling out abruptly.

clue.text: Tent tourists erected proudly every evening, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers put their shelter up with pride each night.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent of the North American Plains peoples.

clue.text: Noted work for malicious lady in California

parts.note: for and to are interchangeable in phrases like a gift for or to someone

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
a cat is a spiteful woman

explanation.surface: A piece written for a spiteful woman living in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted work' is a piece of music, written in notes, not a famous work.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard composition, a musical piece written in notes.

clue.text: Sound record by laic assembly

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: assembly means putting parts together, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A recording made by a lay gathering of churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound in the sense of well-reasoned, as in a sound argument.

clue.text: Specific details about violet's return

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or details

indicators.note: returning means the short name is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: Vi is short for the girl's name Violet

explanation.surface: Particular facts about a flower coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet looks like a flower, but here it is a woman's name, shortened to Vi; 'return' turns that short name round in this down clue before 'about' wraps the details around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Given in the sense of fixed or specified, as in a given time.

clue.text: See anger displayed by a banker

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
ire means anger

explanation.surface: Watch rage shown by a bank employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a crossword joke: a river is something with banks; the clue makes it look like someone in finance.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous French river, and crosswords call any river a banker since it has banks.

clue.text: Anger never found in the free church

definitions.text: never found in the free church
definitions.meaning: the Free Churches, Protestant nonconformists, do not burn perfumed smoke in worship

explanation.walkthrough: The Free Churches are Protestant churches outside the Church of England, such as Methodists and Baptists, whose plain worship avoids ritual smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to enrage, and the fragrant smoke burned in Catholic and High Anglican worship but shunned by nonconformist Free Churches.

clue.text: Leaving little to the imagination!

parts.note: describes skimpy clothing that shows a lot of skin, or a disclosure that tells all

explanation.definitionFit: Describes clothing that exposes much of the body, so onlookers need not guess.

clue.text: Prize won by a lottery backer

indicators.note: a backer here is something going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a draw is a lottery

explanation.surface: A jackpot scooped by someone who bet on a raffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backer' looks like a gambler but tells you to reverse DRAW to WARD; 'won by' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is something given in recognition, a synonym for a trophy.

clue.text: No silver attachment needed on a car

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
plate means silverware or silver-coated items

explanation.surface: No silver trim is required on the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' reads as a negative but is the abbreviation No. for number.
explanation.definitionFit: The registration sign fixed to the front and back of a motor vehicle.
